claim: A debt or hold window that spans a frame wrap loses the lines of the lost frame, so tick the pace clock at least once a frame inside long hooks.

evidence.text: A debt window across a frame wrap lost 311 lines so the wait ran a frame long; K tuning hid it.
A commit over 20 ms lost whole frames until hlib_pace_tick ran per figure.
A 35 ms hook ticked once measured +8.8%; ticking after each long step gave +0.3%.
Without hlib_debt_tick a whole frame of debt was lost in one nest and the run was 36% slow; found by timing the hook's parts.
A full-screen pass ran 70,000 T too long until it read the clock every row.
The debt cap also applies inside a window; capping it low stops nested work counting.
